sights.w: 50-acre rail museum across from Zoo Miami — home of the Ferdinand Magellan, the armoured presidential Pullman used by FDR, Truman, Eisenhower and Reagan; train rides and Florida's largest public model railroad.

sights.address: Miami Executive Airport (Kendall-Tamiami), 14710 SW 128th St, Miami, FL
sights.w: 'Living' aviation museum at the Kendall-Tamiami airport — warbirds that still fly, including a B-26 from the Bay of Pigs invasion.
The original 1936 Parrot Jungle site, now a municipal botanical garden — strangler figs, cypress slough, koi, Swan Lake and the old jungle trails.
515-acre Hialeah park on the old naval air station Earhart flew from — five lakes, the Miami Watersports Complex wakeboard cable, farm village and mountain-bike trails.
Open-air waterfront market on Biscayne Bay — live music daily, bay-cruise docks and the downtown skyline.

sights.address: Watson Island, 1111 Parrot Jungle Trail, Miami, FL
sights.w: 18-acre tropical zoological park on Watson Island — the successor to Parrot Jungle, with sloths, lemurs, flamingos and macaws.
Haitian arts centre with galleries, a 300-seat theatre, the Saturday Caribbean Marketplace and the monthly Big Night in Little Haiti Kreyòl concerts.

sights.address: 1 E Las Olas Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL
sights.w: Broward's flagship art museum on Las Olas — 7,500+ works incl. the largest US collection of CoBrA art and William Glackens; free first Thursdays.
Interactive children's art museum with immersive galleries, now inside Broward Mall in Plantation.
